seo.title: Google Ads Data Strength: Why Tracking Matters
seo.meta_description: Google's October Demand Gen drop focuses on Google Ads data strength, enhanced conversions and Data Manager. What Orange County advertisers should do.

h1: Google Ads Data Strength: Why Better Tracking Means Better Ad Results
answer: Google Ads data strength is about how well your measurement setup feeds campaigns with conversion data. In its October 2026 Demand Gen drop, Google said advertisers who build data strength with Google Tag Gateway see over 20% conversion uplift in Demand Gen on average, and announced a Data Strength Uplift metric. For Anaheim and Orange County advertisers, accurate tracking is the first step to better results.
key_takeaways: Google cites over 20% average conversion uplift with Google Tag Gateway in Demand Gen.
A Data Strength Uplift metric is launching in Google Ads.
Data Manager is expanding to Display & Video 360 and Google Analytics.
Enhanced conversions are coming to Display & Video 360 and Google Analytics.

sections.heading: What Google announced
sections.body_html: On October 13, 2026, Google's October Demand Gen drop focused on data strength, saying Demand Gen is only as powerful as the quality of the data fueling it. Demand Gen campaigns run across Google's visual surfaces, so better measurement helps them find customers.

sections.heading: The headline number
sections.body_html: Google says that, based on internal analysis, advertisers who build their data strength with Google Tag Gateway see, on average, over 20% conversion uplift in Demand Gen campaigns. Google cites its own global performance data from June 2026.

sections.heading: The updates
sections.body_html:
• A Data Strength Uplift metric in Google Ads, showing conversion gains driven by your data setup.
  • Data Manager expanding to Display & Video 360 and Google Analytics, to connect and manage first-party data.
  • Enhanced conversions coming soon to Display & Video 360 and Google Analytics, for more accurate measurement and bidding.

sections.heading: A customer example
sections.body_html: Google says insurance platform The Zebra implemented data strength and achieved a 16% increase in conversion volume and a 19% increase in overall conversion value.

sections.heading: What data strength means for small advertisers
sections.body_html: For a local business, data strength starts with basics: the Google tag installed correctly, the right actions tracked as conversions, and Google Ads linked to Analytics. Without these, smart bidding has little to learn from.

sections.heading: Track the actions that matter
sections.body_html: Mark real lead actions, such as quote requests, bookings and calls, as key events in Google Analytics, and use them as conversions in Google Ads. Page views and clicks alone don't tell campaigns which visitors became customers.

sections.heading: First-party data
sections.body_html: Google points to connecting first-party data, such as customer lists, through Data Manager. Small businesses should only do this in line with their privacy policy and applicable law, and with customers' information handled carefully.

sections.heading: Your setup checklist
sections.body_html:
1. Confirm the Google tag fires on every page.
  2. Define three to five conversion actions that mean real business.
  3. Link Google Ads and Google Analytics.
  4. Ask your developer or agency about enhanced conversions.
  5. Review conversion counts against real leads monthly.

sections.heading: Check the new metric
sections.body_html: When the Data Strength Uplift metric appears in your account, use it to see how much your setup is helping, and fix gaps it highlights.

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.body_html: Imagine a solar installer in Irvine running Demand Gen and Search campaigns that only track page views. It marks consultation requests and qualified calls as conversions, links Ads to Analytics and sets up enhanced conversions with its developer. Bidding starts optimizing toward consultations rather than visits, and the company tracks cost per consultation month over month.

sections.heading: Questions advertisers ask us
sections.body_html: Advertisers often ask what Google Tag Gateway is. It's a Google option for serving the Google tag through your own infrastructure; ask your developer or hosting provider whether it suits your site before changing anything. Another common question is whether small accounts benefit from data strength. Yes: smart bidding works best with accurate conversion data, whatever the budget. Advertisers also ask how to check whether tracking works. Submit a test form, watch it appear in Analytics Realtime and in Google Ads conversions, and compare monthly conversion counts with real leads in your records.

sections.heading: Common tracking problems
sections.body_html: The problems we see most often in Orange County accounts are simple: the Google tag missing from landing pages built in a separate tool, conversions counted twice because both a thank-you page and a form event are tracked, calls not tracked at all, and old conversion actions left active after a website change. Fixing these usually improves data strength more than any new feature.

sections.heading: What Demand Gen campaigns are
sections.body_html: Demand Gen campaigns show ads across Google's visual surfaces to reach people who are browsing and discovering, rather than actively searching. For local businesses, they're often used to build awareness for a new location, a seasonal offer or a service people don't search for until they see it. Because these campaigns rely on Google's systems to find likely customers, the conversion data you provide matters even more than in a simple keyword campaign.

sections.heading: How enhanced conversions help
sections.body_html: Enhanced conversions improve measurement by securely using first-party information that customers provide, such as an email address on a form, to match conversions more accurately. Google says they're coming to Display & Video 360 and Google Analytics. For small advertisers already using Google Ads, ask your developer or agency whether enhanced conversions are set up, and make sure your privacy policy explains how you use customer information. Better matching gives bidding a clearer picture of which ads lead to real customers.

sections.heading: A month-by-month plan
sections.body_html: In the first month, audit tracking: confirm the tag fires everywhere, list your conversion actions, remove duplicates and link Ads with Analytics. In the second month, add missing lead actions such as calls or bookings and ask about enhanced conversions. In the third month, compare conversion counts with real leads and adjust bidding goals to the actions that matter most. Watch the new Data Strength Uplift metric when it appears in your account. This steady approach suits small advertisers in Anaheim and across Orange County better than trying to change everything at once, and it gives each change time to show its effect before the next one. Keep a simple log of every tracking change with the date, so if conversion numbers jump or drop suddenly you can tell whether it's real performance or a measurement change. Share the log with anyone who manages your ads, and review it whenever results change unexpectedly. Good data is never finished; it needs checking every time your website or forms change.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Google Ads data strength means giving campaigns accurate conversion data. Anaheim and Orange County advertisers should fix their tag, track real lead actions, link Ads and Analytics and consider enhanced conversions.

faqs.q: What is Google Ads data strength?
faqs.a: How well your measurement setup feeds campaigns with conversion data.
Over 20% average conversion uplift in Demand Gen with Google Tag Gateway, based on Google's analysis.

faqs.q: What is the Data Strength Uplift metric?
faqs.a: A Google Ads metric showing conversion gains driven by your data setup.
A tool for connecting and managing first-party data, expanding to DV360 and Google Analytics.

faqs.q: Are enhanced conversions coming to Google Analytics?
faqs.a: Google says they'll soon be available in DV360 and Google Analytics.

faqs.q: Where should a small business start?
faqs.a: Correct tagging, real conversion actions and linking Ads with Analytics.

faqs.q: Does more data mean sharing customer details?
faqs.a: Only within your privacy policy and the law; handle customer data carefully.
